sentence: The baker said that she ___ ill.
setupText: On Monday, the baker said, 'I am ill.' She is well again now. Choose the report about her condition on Monday.
taskText: The baker said that she ___ ill.
text: On Monday, the baker said, 'I am ill.' She is well again now. Choose the report about her condition on Monday. The baker said that she ___ ill.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3261:Earlier am statement reported with was
explanation: Was reports the baker's condition at the earlier time when she spoke.

rationales.is: Is presents the illness as current, but this report concerns Monday's condition and she is well now.
rationales.was: Was reports the baker's condition at the earlier time when she spoke.
rationales.be: Be is not a finite past form for this clause.
rationales.were: 'Were' does not agree with singular 'she' in this ordinary past statement.

sentence: The hikers said that they ___ hungry.
setupText: The hikers said, 'We are hungry.' Use a past-tense report about the hikers at that moment.
taskText: The hikers said that they ___ hungry.
text: The hikers said, 'We are hungry.' Use a past-tense report about the hikers at that moment. The hikers said that they ___ hungry.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3262:Plural are-to-were shift in a specified past report
explanation: 'Were' is the past form of 'be' that agrees with the plural subject 'they'.

rationales.was: 'Was' is singular and does not agree with 'they' in this ordinary past statement.
rationales.be: 'Be' needs a finite form in the reported clause.
rationales.were: 'Were' is the past form of 'be' that agrees with the plural subject 'they'.
rationales.is: 'Is' is singular present, not the plural past form requested.

sentence: The waiter said that he ___ at the restaurant.
setupText: Before the restaurant closed, the waiter said, 'I work here.' Report his job at that earlier time.
taskText: The waiter said that he ___ at the restaurant.
text: Before the restaurant closed, the waiter said, 'I work here.' Report his job at that earlier time. The waiter said that he ___ at the restaurant.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3263:Present-simple job statement recast in a past reporting frame
explanation: Worked reports the job he had at the earlier speaking time.

rationales.work: 'Work' does not agree with 'he' and does not supply the requested past form.
rationales.working: 'Working' needs an auxiliary to form a complete clause here.
rationales.is work: Is work incorrectly combines be with the base verb for this meaning.
rationales.worked: Worked reports the job he had at the earlier speaking time.

sentence: The mechanic said that she ___.
setupText: The mechanic said, 'I am repairing the brakes.' Choose the past-continuous report of the work in progress then.
taskText: The mechanic said that she ___.
text: The mechanic said, 'I am repairing the brakes.' Choose the past-continuous report of the work in progress then. The mechanic said that she ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3264:Ongoing activity preserved through am-doing to was-doing reporting
explanation: Was repairing keeps the work in progress at the time the mechanic spoke.

rationales.was repairing the brakes: Was repairing keeps the work in progress at the time the mechanic spoke.
rationales.had repaired the brakes: Had repaired presents the repair as completed earlier rather than in progress then.
rationales.repaired the brakes: Repaired uses a simple whole-event form instead of the requested ongoing past form.
rationales.would repair the brakes: Would repair places the repair ahead of the speaking time rather than in progress at it.

sentence: The swimmer said that she ___.
setupText: The swimmer said, 'I can swim a kilometer.' Use 'could' to report the same ability from that past conversation.
taskText: The swimmer said that she ___.
text: The swimmer said, 'I can swim a kilometer.' Use 'could' to report the same ability from that past conversation. The swimmer said that she ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3265:Could plus base verb in a report of ability
explanation: 'Could' plus the base form 'swim' reports the ability without changing its positive meaning.

rationales.could not swim a kilometer: 'Could not' adds a negative and reverses the stated ability.
rationales.could swim a kilometer: 'Could' plus the base form 'swim' reports the ability without changing its positive meaning.
rationales.could swimming a kilometer: A modal such as 'could' takes the base form 'swim', not 'swimming'.

sentence: The plumber said that he ___.
setupText: The plumber said, 'I will call before I arrive.' Choose the report using 'would' for that future action viewed from the past.
taskText: The plumber said that he ___.
text: The plumber said, 'I will call before I arrive.' Choose the report using 'would' for that future action viewed from the past. The plumber said that he ___.
options: would to call before he arrived
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3266:Will-to-would report with a base-form complement
explanation: 'Would call' keeps the promised call later than the original conversation and uses the required base verb.

rationales.would called before he arrived: 'Would' needs the base form 'call', not the past form 'called'.
rationales.would calling before he arrived: 'Calling' cannot follow 'would' directly in this verb phrase.
rationales.would call before he arrived: 'Would call' keeps the promised call later than the original conversation and uses the required base verb.
rationales.would to call before he arrived: 'Would' does not take 'to' before its main verb.

sentence: She asks me ___.
setupText: The receptionist says to me, 'Please wait by the lift.' Choose the report of her request.
taskText: She asks me ___.
text: The receptionist says to me, 'Please wait by the lift.' Choose the report of her request. She asks me ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3267:Polite request reported with ask plus person plus to-infinitive
explanation: Asks me to wait reports the action she wants me to take.

rationales.wait by the lift: Ask someone needs to before the requested action in this pattern.
rationales.waiting by the lift: Waiting does not form the requested ask-me-to construction.
rationales.that wait by the lift: 'That' cannot introduce this bare command after 'asks me'.
rationales.to wait by the lift: Asks me to wait reports the action she wants me to take.

sentence: The attendant tells us ___.
setupText: A museum attendant tells us, 'Don't touch the glass.' Keep the instruction negative.
taskText: The attendant tells us ___.
text: A museum attendant tells us, 'Don't touch the glass.' Keep the instruction negative. The attendant tells us ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3268:Negative command reported with not to
explanation: 'Not to touch' reports the negative instruction after 'tells us'.

rationales.not to touch the glass: 'Not to touch' reports the negative instruction after 'tells us'.
rationales.to touch the glass: To touch removes the prohibition and tells us to do the opposite.
rationales.not touching the glass: Not touching is not the infinitive complement required in this tell-us instruction pattern.
rationales.don't touch the glass: Don't touch is the direct command; an indirect instruction here uses not to touch.

sentence: The passenger asks ___ the bag is mine.
setupText: A passenger asks me, 'Is this your bag?' Choose the word introducing a reported yes/no question.
taskText: The passenger asks ___ the bag is mine.
text: A passenger asks me, 'Is this your bag?' Choose the word introducing a reported yes/no question. The passenger asks ___ the bag is mine.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3269:If introducing a simple reported yes/no question
explanation: If introduces the question of whether the bag belongs to me.

rationales.that: That introduces a statement here, not the yes/no question being reported.
rationales.if: If introduces the question of whether the bag belongs to me.
rationales.what: What asks for an identity or thing; it does not introduce this yes/no ownership question.
rationales.where: Where asks about a location, which is not what the passenger wants to know.

sentence: The visitor asks ___.
setupText: The visitor asks, 'Where is the cash machine?' Choose standard statement order inside the report.
taskText: The visitor asks ___.
text: The visitor asks, 'Where is the cash machine?' Choose standard statement order inside the report. The visitor asks ___.
options: where does the cash machine is
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3270:Subject-before-be order in a present reported wh-question
explanation: The subject 'the cash machine' comes before 'is' in the reported question.

rationales.where is the cash machine: This keeps direct-question inversion; the indirect question uses the cash machine is.
rationales.where does the cash machine is: 'Does' cannot combine with 'is' in this way, and the embedded question does not need do-support.
rationales.where the cash machine is: The subject 'the cash machine' comes before 'is' in the reported question.
rationales.where the cash machine be: 'Be' is not the finite present form required after this singular subject.

sentence: The colleague asks, 'What is your name?'
setupText: Choose the report matching the new colleague's question to me.
taskText: The colleague asks, 'What is your name?'
text: Choose the report matching the new colleague's question to me. The colleague asks, 'What is your name?'
options: The colleague tells me his name.
The colleague asks me to choose a name.
The colleague asks me my name.
answer: The colleague asks me my name.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3271:Information requested distinguished from information supplied
explanation: Asks me my name reports the information he wants from me.

This makes the colleague give information about himself instead of asking about me.
'Says my name' means he speaks the name, not that he asks what it is.
Asking me to choose a name requests an action different from giving my existing name.
Asks me my name reports the information he wants from me.

sentence: The guest said on Tuesday that he had arrived ___.
setupText: On Tuesday the guest said, 'I arrived yesterday.' Which phrase keeps 'yesterday' linked to the day he spoke?
taskText: The guest said on Tuesday that he had arrived ___.
text: On Tuesday the guest said, 'I arrived yesterday.' Which phrase keeps 'yesterday' linked to the day he spoke? The guest said on Tuesday that he had arrived ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3272:Yesterday reported as the day before the original speech
explanation: 'The day before' refers to Monday, the day before the guest's Tuesday statement.

rationales.the day before: 'The day before' refers to Monday, the day before the guest's Tuesday statement.
rationales.the next day: 'The next day' points forward from Tuesday rather than back to the arrival day.
rationales.on Tuesday: 'On Tuesday' makes arrival happen on the speaking day instead of the previous day.
rationales.the following week: 'The following week' shifts arrival to a later week, not 'yesterday' relative to the conversation.

sentence: The gardener said she would return ___.
setupText: On Friday the gardener said, 'I will return tomorrow.' Report the return relative to that Friday conversation.
taskText: The gardener said she would return ___.
text: On Friday the gardener said, 'I will return tomorrow.' Report the return relative to that Friday conversation. The gardener said she would return ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3273:Tomorrow reported as the next day after speaking
explanation: The next day keeps the return on the day after the gardener spoke.

rationales.the day before: The day before moves the return earlier than the conversation, but tomorrow points forward.
rationales.the next day: The next day keeps the return on the day after the gardener spoke.
rationales.earlier that week: Earlier that week places the return before Friday, reversing the future reference.
rationales.on Thursday: Thursday is before the Friday conversation, not its tomorrow.

sentence: The owner said he lived ___.
setupText: At the harbor the boat owner said, 'I live here.' Later, from another town, report where the owner lives using a place name.
taskText: The owner said he lived ___.
text: At the harbor the boat owner said, 'I live here.' Later, from another town, report where the owner lives using a place name. The owner said he lived ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3274:Here resolved to the original speaking place
explanation: 'Here' in the original harbor conversation refers to the harbor, so naming it preserves the location.

rationales.in the other town: The other town is the later reporter's location, not the location of the owner's here.
rationales.where I live now: The owner's here refers to where he spoke, not automatically to where the reporter now lives.
rationales.at the harbor: 'Here' in the original harbor conversation refers to the harbor, so naming it preserves the location.
rationales.wherever his listener lives: A speaker's 'here' does not mean any place a listener happens to live.

sentence: I said that ___ needed a larger size.
setupText: I said, 'I need a larger size.' I am now reporting my own words.
taskText: I said that ___ needed a larger size.
text: I said, 'I need a larger size.' I am now reporting my own words. I said that ___ needed a larger size.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3275:First person retained in a self-report
explanation: I stays I because the original speaker and the reporter are the same person.

rationales.she: She introduces a different person; I am reporting my own need.
rationales.he: He would also change the person who needs the larger size.
rationales.they: They replaces the original speaker with another person or group.
rationales.I: I stays I because the original speaker and the reporter are the same person.

sentence: The guests say that ___ room is quiet.
setupText: Two guests say, 'Our room is quiet.' I do not share their room. Keep the ownership clear in my report.
taskText: The guests say that ___ room is quiet.
text: Two guests say, 'Our room is quiet.' I do not share their room. Keep the ownership clear in my report. The guests say that ___ room is quiet.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3276:Plural possessive our reported as their by an outsider
explanation: 'Their' refers to the room belonging to the two guests in the message.

rationales.their: 'Their' refers to the room belonging to the two guests in the message.
rationales.our: Our would include me as a person sharing the room, contrary to the context.
rationales.my: My would make the room mine alone instead of the guests'.
rationales.his: His changes a two-person possession into one man's possession.

sentence: During a walk, my friend says, 'Let's stop for a rest.'
setupText: Choose the report that matches a suggestion to do something together.
taskText: During a walk, my friend says, 'Let's stop for a rest.'
text: Choose the report that matches a suggestion to do something together. During a walk, my friend says, 'Let's stop for a rest.'
options: My friend refuses to stop for a rest.
My friend says we have already rested.
My friend asks why I rested.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3277:Let's recognized as a shared suggestion
explanation: Let's stop proposes a shared action, so suggests a rest captures its purpose.

'Refuses' would mean the friend does not agree to stop, the opposite of the suggestion.
Let's stop proposes a shared action, so suggests a rest captures its purpose.
'Have already rested' describes a completed event instead of suggesting a new rest.
Why I rested asks about a reason for an earlier action, not a shared next step.

sentence: The passenger ___.
setupText: A fellow passenger sees my heavy case and says, 'I'll carry it for you.' Choose the report of this offer.
taskText: The passenger ___.
text: A fellow passenger sees my heavy case and says, 'I'll carry it for you.' Choose the report of this offer. The passenger ___.
options: asked me to carry his case
asked whether I owned a case
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3278:Volunteered help reported as an offer
explanation: Offered to carry reports the passenger's volunteered help with my case.

rationales.asked me to carry his case: This reverses both the helper and the owner of the case.
rationales.refused to carry my case: Refused contradicts the passenger's willingness to help.
rationales.offered to carry my case: Offered to carry reports the passenger's volunteered help with my case.
rationales.asked whether I owned a case: The passenger offers help rather than asking a question about ownership.

sentence: The trainer ___ the session was free.

taskText: The trainer ___ the session was free.
text: Choose the natural pattern with 'told' and a named listener. The trainer ___ the session was free.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3279:Complete told plus listener plus that-clause pattern
explanation: 'Told us that' names the listeners and introduces the information they received.

rationales.told that: In this use of 'tell', the report needs a listener, such as 'us', before 'that'.
rationales.told us to that: 'To' cannot stand between 'us' and a 'that' clause in this pattern.
rationales.told us that: 'Told us that' names the listeners and introduces the information they received.

sentence: The guide says that the river ___.
setupText: A guide says, 'The river runs through the city.' The report begins with 'says', not 'said'.
taskText: The guide says that the river ___.
text: A guide says, 'The river runs through the city.' The report begins with 'says', not 'said'. The guide says that the river ___.
focusKey: coverage-reported-speech-a2-3280:Present factual verb retained after present says
explanation: 'Runs' agrees with 'the river' and keeps the present fact after the present reporting verb 'says'.

rationales.runs through the city: 'Runs' agrees with 'the river' and keeps the present fact after the present reporting verb 'says'.
rationales.run through the city: 'Run' lacks the singular -s required with the river in this present statement.
rationales.running through the city: 'Running' needs an auxiliary to form a complete verb phrase here.
rationales.is run through the city: 'Is run' is a passive form, which does not express the river's ordinary course through the city.
